facts.statement: The genus was named after Nikolai Nikolaevich Bogolubov, who discovered the remains in 1914.
facts.quote: It is named for Nikolai Nikolaevich Bogolubov, the paleontologist who discovered the remains in 1914.

facts.statement: This pterosaur lived during the early Campanian stage of the Upper Cretaceous in the Rybushka Formation of Petrovsk, Saratov Oblast, Russia.
facts.quote: Bogolubovia is a genus of pterosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (early Campanian) Rybushka Formation of Petrovsk, Saratov Oblast, Russia.

facts.statement: The original specimen, which consisted of a single partial large cervical vertebra, was initially assigned to the species Ornithostoma orientalis.
facts.quote: Bogolubov had initially assigned the specimen, consisting of a single partial large cervical vertebra, as a new species of Ornithostoma, O. orientalis.

facts.statement: The species was later reclassified as Pteranodon before being moved to its own genus within the family Pteranodontidae by Nessov and Yarkov in 1989.
facts.quote: It was later reclassified as a species of Pteranodon, before being reassigned to a separate genus of Pteranodontidae by Lev Nessov and Alexander Yarkov in 1989.

facts.statement: In 2008, some researchers considered Bogolubovia a nomen dubium that might be identical to the genus Volgadraco.
facts.quote: In 2008, however, it was considered to be a nomen dubium that might in fact be identical to the genus Volgadraco, another pterosaur from Russia.

facts.statement: In 2020, Averianov and Arkhangelsky suggested that Bogolubovia is likely a valid pteranodontid based on similarities to Volgadraco.
facts.quote: In 2020, Averianov and Arkhangelsky suggested that the cervical vertebrae of Bogolubovia is similar to that of Volgadraco, reconsidered as a pteranodontid, and thus this genus is likely a pteranodontid.

facts.statement: New remains described in 2022 suggested that both Bogolubovia and Volgadraco are valid species of pteranodontids.
facts.quote: New remains described in 2022 suggested that Bogulobovia and Volgadraco were both valid species of pteranodontids.

facts.statement: In 1991, the genus was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae, though Wellnhofer retained it as a Pteranodontidae.
facts.quote: Fue asignado en 1991 a la familia Azhdarchidae. Wellnhofer (1991) sin embargo, lo retuvo como un Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: The fossil record for this genus spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: It was a mid-sized pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of 3 to 4 meters based on the holotype, while a later found radius suggests a wingspan of 4.3 meters.
rejected.quote: Bogolubovia would have been a mid-sized pterosaur, with an estimated wingspan of 3 - 4 m suggested by the holotype; a later found radius indicates a wingspan of 4.3 m.
